From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese jazer, from Latin jacēre, iacēre (“to lie prostrate”), from Proto-Italic *jakēō. Compare Spanish yacer, French gésir and Italian giacere.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ʒaˈze(ʁ)/ [ʒaˈze(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ʒaˈze(ʁ)/ [ʒaˈze(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /ʒaˈze(ɾ)/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ʒaˈze(ʁ)/ [ʒaˈze(χ)]
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ʒaˈze(ɻ)/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ʒɐˈzeɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ʒɐˈzeɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /ʒɐˈze.ɾi/

  • Hyphenation: ja‧zer

Verb

[edit]

jazer (first-person singular present jazo, first-person singular preterite jazi, past participle jazido) (archaic)

  1. (intransitive) to lie, to sit (be situated)
    Synonym: estar
  2. (intransitive) to lay, to lie down
    Synonym: estar deitado
